newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Lesotho police rebels seek asylum in S.Africa.
newsitem.headline: Lesotho police rebels seek asylum in S.Africa.

text.p: Two rebel policemen from Lesotho who fled to South Africa after a police mutiny was crushed by armed forces have applied for political asylum, a foreign affairs spokesman said on Saturday.

"They have been interviewed by the Department of Home Affairs. They have been in touch with home affairs in connection with an application for asylum and we have been in touch with home affairs," foreign affairs spokesman Pieter Swanepoel told Reuters.
Swanepoel said Second-Lieutenant Phakiso Molise and Sergeant Motlatsi Makateng were in South Africa, but he did not know where they were staying.
Molise and seven other policemen started the mutiny when they seized the Lesotho police headquarters in February and refused to be arrested for the alleged killing of three fellow officers in 1995.
The mutiny ended when the Lesotho army raided the police building and arrested 100 policemen who had taken part.
Molise managed to escape and hid at the palace of Lesotho King Letsie III before fleeing across the border to South Africa.

Lesotho's deputy prime minister and minister in charge of police, Pakalitha Mosisili said in the kingdom's capital Maseru on Friday the rebel leader had sought political asylum at the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) in Pretoria.
UNHCR spokesman Yusuf Hassan denied the men were with the U.N. agency.
